description:
Release bookkeeping in this repo has drifted from the actual published
state, in two independent ways confirmed against the repo and PyPI on
2026-07-03:

1. `CHANGELOG.md` line 10 has a `## [0.3.1] - 2026-05-30` section written
   in the same released-version format as every other dated entry (e.g.
   `## [0.3.0] - 2026-05-16` at line 53), but no `v0.3.1` git tag exists
   (`git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v0.3.*'` returns only
   `refs/tags/v0.3.0`) and PyPI has never served `0.3.1`
   (`pip index versions benchbox` lists `0.3.0` as latest). The section
   reads as shipped when it is not.

2. `README.md:31` says `Current release: v0.2.1`, but that has been stale
   since `v0.3.0` published; PyPI-latest is `0.3.0`, not `0.2.1`
   (`pyproject.toml` and `benchbox/__init__.py` also still read `0.2.1`
   on `develop`, which is expected per the release-cut flow in
   `Makefile:977-1057` — version bumps happen only on the ephemeral
   release branch, not on `develop` — but README's human-facing claim
   needs to reflect the actual latest published release, not develop's
   working version file).

Compounding both: `v0.3.0` is PyPI-latest but fails a clean import
(`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'`, reverified live via
`uv run --isolated --no-project --with 'benchbox==0.3.0' -- python -c
'import benchbox'` run from outside the repo tree). So the CHANGELOG
currently implies a working, released `0.3.1` fix exists when the
PyPI-latest install is actually broken.

This TODO owns the honesty fix to the release bookkeeping (CHANGELOG
wording/dating, README's current-release line) and a durable guard so a
`CHANGELOG.md` released-version section can never again claim a version
with no corresponding git tag. It does NOT own cutting the real `v0.3.1`
release — that belongs to `release-recovery-v0-3-1`, which is already
Critical priority and already in flight.

anti_patterns.instead: move/re-date it instead of dropping it.
anti_patterns.why: it documents real completed work (pandas lazy-loading, Databricks Liquid Clustering, etc.) that will ship in the eventual recovery release

anti_patterns.dont: hardcode a new version string guess into README.md without checking PyPI
anti_patterns.instead: verify against pip index versions benchbox or the release tag list before writing a version number.
anti_patterns.why: that recreates the exact drift this TODO fixes

anti_patterns.dont: make the w4 guard block make release-cut's own changelog draft
anti_patterns.instead: scope the check to already-merged develop/main state, not the release branch mid-flight.
anti_patterns.why: that draft legitimately claims an untagged version before the tag is pushed

work_units.notes:
Capture compact evidence (do not commit raw logs):
  - `git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v0.3.*'` -> only v0.3.0
  - `uv run --isolated --with pip -- python -m pip index versions benchbox`
    -> LATEST: 0.3.0
  - `cd /tmp && uv run --isolated --no-project --with 'benchbox==0.3.0' --
    python -c 'import benchbox'` -> ModuleNotFoundError: pandas
    (run from outside the repo tree — running from the repo root
    silently shadows the installed wheel with the local `benchbox/`
    source directory and gives a false pass)
  - `grep -n 'Current release' README.md` -> still v0.2.1
If any of these have changed (e.g. v0.3.1 has since actually
shipped), stop and re-scope this TODO against deps.needs before
editing CHANGELOG/README.
work_units.summary: Re-validate the cited drift facts before editing

work_units.notes:
Two acceptable outcomes depending on w1's findings; pick one and
say which in the PR body:
  (a) If v0.3.1 has not shipped yet: move the `[0.3.1] - 2026-05-30`
      content under `## [Unreleased]` (merging with any existing
      Unreleased content) and drop the specific date, since dated
      sections are a released-version convention elsewhere in this
      file (`0.3.0`, `0.2.1`, etc.).
  (b) If the plan is still to cut a real v0.3.1 imminently: keep the
      section but re-date it to `TBD` or the actual cut date once
      known, and do not let a future-dated or past-but-unreleased
      date sit in a released-version slot.
Either way, add a short note under the entry (or a new `0.3.0`
addendum) that `0.3.0` shipped with a broken clean install
(`ModuleNotFoundError: pandas`) and that the fix is pending release,
consistent with the honest state release-recovery-v0-3-1 is working
toward.
work_units.summary: Fix CHANGELOG.md so the 0.3.1 section cannot be read as released

Extend `scripts/generate_changelog_entry.py` (which already knows how
to detect the latest `v*` tag via `git describe --tags --abbrev=0

out-of-tree module-loading pattern used for `_project/scripts`
modules — decide whether this check belongs in `scripts/` or
`_project/scripts/` based on where it needs to run: CI content-guard
vs. one-off release tooling).

The check: parse `CHANGELOG.md` for `## [X.Y.Z] - <date>` headers
(excluding `[Unreleased]`) and assert each `X.Y.Z` has a
corresponding `vX.Y.Z` tag reachable from `git tag -l` / `git
ls-remote --tags origin`. Wire it into `make pr-preflight` or the
content-guard path (whichever this repo already uses for
CHANGELOG-adjacent lint) so a future premature dated section fails
CI instead of silently drifting again.
work_units.summary: Add a guard: a CHANGELOG released-version section requires a matching git tag
